mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates economic weakness, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, thus driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production index by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening economy, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a month signals economic strength, leading to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thus driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) both increase by more than 1% in a month, it signals a strengthening consumer demand, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST, RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with high interest rates
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint correlation between high FEDFUNDS, increasing CPIAUCSL and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals economic strength, leading to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thus driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
